title: Counter loop completion segment
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, state $a$, designated exit state or halting exit, and let $e:\\{0,1\\}\\hookrightarrow\\Gamma$ encode Boolean symbols in its alphabet. Let $w$ be a Boolean word whose binary value is $d$, and suppose the extra tape initially stores the encoded word at cells $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$: for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$, its content at $cp+p$ equals the word-buffer content at $p$. Let $c$ be an initial configuration and let $P$ be a property of the $k$ work-head positions, with $P$ true at $c$. Suppose that for each $r<d$, the $r$th iterate of the variable-length run of $M$ from $c$ to its next round has a round of length $\\tau$, satisfies the round conditions for exit set $\\{exit\\}$ and property $P$, and ends in state $a$. Then the counter-loop machine that runs $M$ on the first $k$ tapes and uses the encoded extra tape for its counter reaches its done configuration after $\\sum_{r<d}\\tau(c_r)+\\operatorname{overhead}(w,d+1)$ steps, where $c_r$ is the $r$th round configuration and the counter tape has been filled with encoded true symbols on the cells $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$. Before that time its state is neither done nor escape; throughout the segment the extra head stays in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and $P$ holds for the first $k$ head positions. Here a segment means the stated endpoint is reached, no state in $\\{done,escape\\}$ occurs earlier, and the position condition holds at every time up to and including the endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: Counter word $w$ and its binary value $d$
Initial extra-tape buffer agreement for all $-1\\le p\\le |w|$
Each round $r<d$ satisfies the round conditions and ends in state $a' = a$
